headline: Choose factors in nondecreasing order to avoid permutations
statement: Return every unordered factorization of n using at least two factors, each between 2 and n-1. Represent a combination in nondecreasing order; combinations may be returned in any order.
intuition: Build a factorization in increasing order. Try a divisor of the amount still left, pair it with the remaining quotient, and then try splitting that quotient further. Starting later choices at the current divisor avoids repeating the same factors in different orders.
approach: Search factors from a minimum allowed factor through sqrt(remaining).
For each divisor f, emit path + [f, remaining//f].
Recurse on the quotient with minimum factor f to allow repeats without decreasing order.
correctness: Every emitted list multiplies to n and has at least two factors. Nondecreasing choices make each unordered factorization unique. Any factorization with at least two factors has a smallest factor no greater than sqrt(remaining), which the loop reaches; recursion lists all decompositions of the quotient.
bruteForce: List sequences of candidate integers and multiply them, generating many permutations and impossible products.

complexity.time: Output-sensitive search; divisor scans cost O(sqrt(r)) per remaining product r
complexity.explanation: Time Output-sensitive search; divisor scans cost O(sqrt(r)) per remaining product r; additional space O(log n) recursion excluding output. Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: Keep the same minimum factor after selecting f so repeated factors are legal.
n=1 and primes have no factorizations.
